must_have: The article title explicitly identifies the study as randomized/randomised or uses an unambiguous lexical variant identifying random allocation.
not_if: The text is not the article title; do not assign item 1a to abstract, Methods, Results, or Discussion text.
The title refers to a trial or study but does not explicitly identify randomization.
The title reports control, placebo, masking, protocol, pilot, or other design features without explicit randomization.
The text describes random-sequence generation; assign 8a when applicable.
The text describes allocation restriction, stratification, blocking, or minimisation; assign 8b when applicable.
The text describes trial design or setting in Methods; assign 3a or other applicable Methods items.
The text concerns abstract reporting or trial registration; assign the applicable abstract or registration item instead.
1a.definition: Identification as a randomised trial in the title

must_have: A substantive sentence in the Abstract
The abstract as a whole is structured
Trial design is summarized
Methods are summarized
Results are summarized
Conclusions are summarized
not_if: No abstract is present
The abstract lacks a structured trial summary
Header-only text is present
An isolated setting statement supports 4b
An isolated registration statement supports 23
Trial identification in title supports 1a
Design details alone support 3a
Non-abstract summary text is present
Objectives alone support 2b
Outcome results alone support 17a
Harms alone support 19
Funding alone supports 25
1b.definition: Structured summary of trial design, methods, results, and conclusions

must_have: Substantive scientific or clinical context about the condition, intervention, comparison, or clinical problem that helps explain why the trial was needed
Or a prospective explanatory or pragmatic rationale for undertaking the trial, such as an evidence gap, unmet need, uncertainty, plausible pretrial mechanism, or anticipated benefit-harm question
The sentence must function as background or pretrial justification, rather than as a study aim, procedural detail, result, or post-trial interpretation
not_if: It only states an objective, research question, or hypothesis without substantive background or rationale (2b)
It only describes design, eligibility, allocation, intervention procedures, outcome definitions, or follow-up (3a-11b, especially 6a)
It only describes statistical methods or modelling choices (12a)
Its primary function is reporting results, effect estimates, subgroup findings, or observed comparisons (17a)
It interprets trial findings, discusses implications, or offers post hoc mechanistic explanations (22)
It is only a heading, label, vague promotional claim, or unsupported importance assertion
2a.definition: Scientific background and explanation of rationale

must_have: A specific objective, research question, comparison purpose, or hypothesis for the randomized trial.
The statement identifies a substantive intervention, comparison, effect, relationship, feasibility determination, estimate, or other concrete evaluand relevant to the trial.

The objective may be explicit, prospectively framed, stated as a completed assessment, or expressed through planned trial testing or an expected intervention effect that makes the intended determination clear.
A sentence may qualify through immediate local context when an adjacent statement explicitly supplies the trial objective or hypothesis and the sentence clearly advances that same purpose.
A multiarm design does not by itself require a separately stated hypothesis or explicit mapping of every objective to every group.
not_if: Do not assign for background rationale, prior evidence, clinical uncertainty, or a general need for evidence without a stated, clearly referenced, or locally completed trial objective or hypothesis; use item 2a when applicable.
Do not assign for a generic intention to investigate, evaluate outcomes, or address uncertainty when the substantive intervention, effect, endpoint, or determination is not identifiable.

Do not assign for hypotheses about observational associations, biological mechanisms, or non-trial relationships unless they explicitly state the purpose or hypothesis of the randomized trial evaluation.
Do not assign for outcome definitions, measurement procedures, follow-up descriptions, or endpoint lists without a trial purpose or hypothesis; use item 6a when applicable.
Do not assign for statistical procedures, diagnostic-performance analyses, model specifications, or analysis plans that do not state the substantive trial question; use item 12a when applicable.
Do not assign for observed effects or group differences reported as findings rather than as a stated objective or hypothesis; use item 18 when applicable.
Do not assign for a bare heading or label without accompanying substantive objective content.

must_have: An explicit designation of the overall study or trial design, including a recognized design subtype, broad trial label, phase, pilot framing, comparative design framework, or named design structure.
or an explicit description of the study-period framework that characterizes the design, such as planned run-in, treatment, crossover, or follow-up periods.
or an explicit reference to a figure, table, diagram, or schema that is itself identified as presenting the study design.

An allocation ratio supports item 3a only when the same evidence also independently provides an overall design designation or design framework; a ratio alone is not sufficient under the observed annotation policy.
not_if: Only reports random sequence generation or assignment mechanics, including a standalone allocation ratio; assign 8a when applicable.
Only reports blocking, stratification, or other randomisation restrictions without an explicit overall design designation or design framework; assign 8b when applicable.
Only reports allocation concealment or assignment implementation; assign 9 when applicable.
Only identifies personnel responsible for generation, enrollment, or assignment; assign 10 when applicable.
Only reports masking procedures or who was blinded, without a trial-design designation or design-period framework; assign 11a when applicable.
Only reports intervention delivery, treatment arms, doses, or comparator content without a design-level characterization; assign 5 when applicable.
Only reports a post-commencement design modification without describing the original design; assign 3b when applicable.
Only states that the study has multiple parts, without naming a design type or describing the design framework.
Only describes eligibility for comparisons or participation in comparisons, without an explicit design designation.
A figure or table reference alone does not qualify unless the artifact or caption is explicitly identified as a study-design display.
3a.definition: Description of trial design (such as parallel, factorial) including allocation ratio

must_have: An explicitly enacted trial-level or arm-level modification after trial commencement affecting conduct, intervention, recruitment, eligibility, procedures, randomisation, design, or analysis methods
Either the enacted change itself or an unambiguously linked local rationale, trigger, or consequence for that enacted change
Evidence that the statement concerns a later modification rather than an original planned method

For analysis methods, a newly adopted or revised analysis specification with temporal or contextual evidence that it was introduced after trial commencement; this may be co-labelled with 6b when relevant
not_if: Initial design, regimen, allocation, follow-up, centre procedure, or analysis plan with no later modification; use 3a where applicable
Initial eligibility specification with no later revision; use 4a
An outcome-only revision with no broader implemented methods change; use 6b
A planned interim procedure or prespecified adaptive feature that was not actually modified; use 7b where applicable
Whole-trial early closure without a reported arm, intervention, procedure, or design modification; use 14b
An isolated participant deviation without a systematic trial-level or arm-level conduct change
Routine statistical reporting, post-hoc analysis, or original analysis-plan description without evidence of a revised or newly adopted post-start analysis method; use 12a where applicable
A mere protocol reference without an actual amendment signal or a linked amendment rationale
A rationale or trigger statement that cannot be locally linked to an enacted trial-level or arm-level modification
3b.definition: Important changes to methods after trial commencement (such as eligibility criteria), with reasons

must_have: An explicit inclusion, exclusion, enrolment, screening, or randomisation condition that determines who may enter the trial or a specified randomised comparison.

The condition may concern demographics, diagnosis, presenting condition, disease severity, clinical status, geography, care pathway, prior or concomitant treatment, treatment failure, treatment stability, timing, consent, or another participant-selection factor.

A recruitment, enrolment, or trial-population statement may satisfy the item when it identifies the selected participants by a condition such as diagnosis, severity, presenting condition, or prior-treatment history, even if formal inclusion or exclusion terminology is absent.

A mandatory medication washout, cessation, or stability requirement is eligibility when it must be met before screening, enrolment, or randomisation in order to enter the trial or the relevant comparison.

Alternatively, an explicit statement that the trial's inclusion or exclusion criteria are reported in a cited protocol, publication, or external source is sufficient when it clearly directs the reader to those criteria; a bare heading alone is insufficient.
not_if: It reports recruitment sources, settings, locations, or timing without a condition determining participant eligibility; assign 4b for study settings or locations.
It reports only a post-commencement eligibility amendment; assign 3b.
It gives dosing, administration, withholding, switching, permitted medication use, or monitoring instructions after enrolment without making them pre-entry conditions; assign 5 when applicable.
It describes a run-in purpose or screening process without stating a condition that participants must satisfy to proceed.
It reports consent having been obtained, signed, or documented without stating that consent was required for enrolment.
It defines a diagnosis, infection, laboratory state, or case classification without linking that definition to selecting, recruiting, enrolling, or randomising participants.

It gives a threshold, diagnosis, or clinical status solely for a later randomisation, treatment phase, allocation pathway, or subgroup assignment rather than entry into the trial or the specified comparison; assign 10 when applicable.
It reports observed participant characteristics or between-group baseline comparisons rather than selection criteria; assign 15 when applicable.
It reports screened, excluded, randomised, analysed, completed, or lost participant numbers without stating an eligibility condition; consider 13a, 13b, or 16.
It reports recruitment dates or follow-up timing without an eligibility condition; assign 14a.
It only names a participant or eligibility subsection without reporting criteria or clearly directing the reader to reported criteria elsewhere.
It describes masking or treatment-allocation access without an eligibility condition; assign 11a when applicable.

must_have: Explicitly reports a trial-linked care setting, geographic location, participating site, centre count, or country-level recruitment location.
The reported setting must identify where participants were encountered or where trial recruitment, screening, enrolment, treatment, assessment, or follow-up occurred.
Actual participating centres or sites qualify when tied to trial conduct, recruitment activity, enrolment, activation, or participation status.

A setting report remains eligible when combined with dates, enrolment counts, eligibility language, or trial-design information, provided an actual location, care environment, site, or centre is explicitly stated.
Structured abstract fields and immediately linked tables or figures qualify only when they explicitly state the trial setting or location.
not_if: Do not assign for participant eligibility alone; use 4a when no actual care setting or study location is reported.
Do not assign for site capability requirements, organisational prerequisites, or hypothetical hospital characteristics without identification of actual trial sites.
Do not assign for recruitment, enrolment, treatment, or follow-up dates alone without a stated location, setting, site, or centre; use 14a when applicable.
Do not assign for multicentre design terminology alone without actual site, centre-count, location, or care-context information; use 3a.
Do not assign for treatment procedures, provider decisions, or management logistics that do not identify a participant-facing setting or study organisation; use 5.
Do not assign laboratory, department, or institutional affiliation when it identifies only assay, measurement, or analysis performance; use 6a when applicable.
Do not assign general geographic background unrelated to trial conduct or participants.
Do not assign subsection labels, site labels, or repeated provenance text in non-report contexts without substantive setting information.
Do not assign baseline, outcome, or analysis statements unless their linked display explicitly reports the trial setting or location.
4b.definition: Settings and locations where the data were collected

must_have: Explicitly identify a trial intervention, control, treatment restriction, concomitant-treatment rule, usual-care procedure, or trial-mandated treatment procedure linked to an arm or clear trial-treatment context.

Report at least one intervention-defining element, such as treatment identity, treatment level, regimen type, component, formulation, dose, route, timing, duration, administration instruction, adjustment rule, withholding rule, delivery trigger, treatment condition, or actual exposure.
A named treatment contrast, control formulation, crossover exposure, or regimen may be sufficient even without numeric dose or schedule detail when treatment context is explicit.

For combined interventions, capture stated components, fixed-dose combinations, delivery conditions, or treatment phases; a sentence may describe only one arm, component, contingency, or phase when context establishes the regimen.

Immediate local context may establish the intervention identity or arm: assign when a sentence linked to nearby text, a table, caption, or arm label reports exposure, treatment-associated management, a treatment condition, or a regimen-defining action.
Include permitted, prohibited, required-stable, or adjusted concomitant treatments when they govern treatment delivery during the trial.
Include actual administered or received dose, frequency, duration, or exposure reported in Results when it describes what participants received rather than only adherence totals.
not_if: Do not assign for allocation, randomisation, ratio, blocking, concealment, or assignment language alone when no intervention, treatment contrast, regimen, or control is identified; use items 3a, 8a, 8b, 9, 10, or 13a as applicable.
Do not assign for eligibility or baseline criteria alone; use item 4a, unless the criterion triggers, modifies, limits, permits, or withholds treatment delivery during the trial.
Do not assign for outcome definitions, endpoint schedules, sample handling, laboratory processing, wearable-device use, or assessment procedures that are solely measurement-related; use item 6a.
Do not assign for follow-up contacts, reminders, clinic attendance, diary collection, or retention procedures that only collect outcome data; use item 6a or relevant follow-up reporting.
Do not assign for pre-assessment restrictions or challenge preparation when they standardize testing conditions rather than trial treatment delivery; use item 6a when measurement-related.
Do not assign for statements solely about blinding personnel; use item 11a.

Do not assign for statements solely about identical appearance, matching administration, or placebo use for blinding; use item 11b. Assign item 5 only when formulation, treatment role, or regimen is independently described beyond the blinding function.

Do not assign for allocation-pack preparation, pharmacy workflow, or concealment procedures whose primary role is implementation of assignment; use item 9 or 10 unless the sentence independently states the regimen actually prescribed or administered.

Do not assign for participant flow, adherence totals, discontinuation counts, or generic exposure summaries without dose, regimen, timing, route, or another treatment-delivery detail; use items 13a, 13b, 16, or relevant results items.

Do not assign for unplanned arm termination, supply interruption, temporary suspension, or premature stopping reported as a post-commencement protocol change or flow event; use item 3b or 13b as applicable.
Do not assign for harms or treatment effects alone; use item 19 unless the statement also reports intervention delivery or administration.
Do not assign for generic headings or generic mentions of treatment, control, or usual care without identifying what was given, restricted, prepared, managed, or done.
5.definition: The interventions for each group with sufficient details to allow replication, including how and when they were actually administered

must_have: The text identifies a pre-specified or intended outcome, endpoint-like construct, measurable response, clinical event, disease status, safety event, or feasibility measure for the trial.

OR it describes a planned procedure for determining such an outcome, including diagnostic confirmation, clinical surveillance, examination, laboratory assay, imaging, diary, monitoring, assessor review, scheduled visit, or follow-up process.

A named test, assay, or assessment schedule may qualify without an explicit outcome label when Methods, abstract, or immediately adjacent text makes clear that it determines trial efficacy, safety, clinical status, or an endpoint.

Outcome-assay workflow details, including specimen processing, quality control, assay ordering, and measurement-quality criteria, qualify only when linked to outcome ascertainment rather than general laboratory operations.
A heading, list item, or sentence fragment may qualify when contiguous text supplies its diagnostic definition, measurement method, or timing.
Timing, scale details, thresholds, and primary/secondary labels are included when stated but are not required for every annotation.
The content must describe planned or protocol-relevant measurement or ascertainment; objective-style wording can qualify if it identifies a concrete measurable response, event, or status.
not_if: A purely abstract objective, research question, or hypothesis provides no concrete measurable response, event, status, or ascertainment target (2b).
The text reports a post-commencement change to trial outcomes, outcome definitions, or their rationale (6b).

The text solely describes an analysis model, statistical test, subgroup analysis, score derivation, recoding, data transformation, or analytic exclusion without defining what was measured or how/when it was ascertained (12a or 12b).

The text solely reports observed values, effect estimates, significance findings, between-group comparisons, or Results-only bedside observations without planned outcome-definition content (17a or 17b).
The text solely reports observed adverse-event frequencies or comparative harms results without planned safety monitoring or outcome definition (19).
A masking statement alone does not define an outcome or ascertainment procedure; assign 11a when it only concerns blinding of assessors.
Treatment-administration observation, infusion monitoring, routine care, or operational protocol surveillance is not 6a unless it is explicitly used to determine a trial outcome or safety endpoint.
A bare operational visit, test, or laboratory procedure with no contextual link to endpoint, safety, efficacy, disease-status, or outcome ascertainment is not sufficient.
6a.definition: Completely defined pre-specified primary and secondary outcome measures, including how and when they were assessed

must_have: An actual, explicitly reported modification, amendment, replacement, addition, removal, redesignation, or late specification affecting a trial outcome, endpoint, outcome definition, measurement, coding, ascertainment, or prespecified outcome analysis.
The report must establish that the outcome-related change was enacted after trial commencement; wording such as new, additional, or unplanned alone is insufficient.
A statement may carry 6b through surrounding amendment or change context when it identifies the affected outcome component, even if it does not restate the full change narrative.
A reason for the modification is relevant when reported, but is not required for assignment.
not_if: The statement only defines planned primary or secondary outcomes without a modification or amendment context (6a).
The statement calls an outcome new, additional, or unplanned but does not explicitly establish an enacted outcome-plan change (6a, 12b, or 18 as applicable).
The statement uses an outcome for sample-size planning or calculation without explicitly reporting a changed outcome designation or outcome plan (7a).
The statement concerns a non-outcome protocol change, including eligibility, intervention, recruitment, randomisation, or allocation procedures (3b).
The statement gives ordinary statistical methods, software, models, or tests without modifying an outcome-related prespecified analysis or outcome operationalisation (12a).

The statement reports additional, subgroup, adjusted, exploratory, or post-hoc analyses without changing the outcome construct, collection plan, designation, or prespecified outcome analysis (12b or 18).
The statement only cites or compares a protocol, registry, or analysis plan and identifies no amendment, discrepancy, late specification, or contextually established outcome modification.
The statement reports outcome results, observed biological changes, event rates, or endpoint performance without an outcome-related protocol modification (18).
The statement only describes planned assessment timing, analytic exclusions, or data handling without evidence that the outcome plan itself was modified (6a or 12a).
6b.definition: Any changes to trial outcomes after the trial commenced, with reasons

must_have: An explicit current prospective statement of how the sample size was determined, calculated, justified, or set.
Or an explicitly planned sample target, protocol-defined recruitment cap, or stopping condition that establishes the intended sample size.

Or a substantive sizing input, such as power, precision, effect size, outcome rate, variability, attrition, or source-based rationale, only when the sentence explicitly identifies it as part of the current sample-size calculation or determination.
A reassessed calculation input can qualify when explicitly tied to the sample-size calculation, including when reassessment occurs during recruitment or interim review.
A full formula, target number, allocation ratio, and complete assumptions are not required together, but the sentence must directly connect its information to sample-size determination.
not_if: Only reports numbers enrolled, randomised, analysed, retained, or completed without a prospective sizing rationale or planned target (items 13a, 16).
Only reports a detectable difference, limited power, or inability to detect an effect without an explicit sample-size calculation, target-setting statement, or sizing rationale.
Only gives a prior-study result, assumed value, variability estimate, or anticipated effect without explicitly linking it to the current sample-size calculation.
Only defines an outcome comparison, treatment contrast, measurement, statistical method, or test without prospective sizing context (items 6a, 12a).
Only reports observed imprecision, confidence intervals, limitations, or post hoc power without the original prospective determination (items 17a, 20).
Only describes interim monitoring, stopping rules, or analysis boundaries without a planned sample target or an explicit sample-size calculation input (item 7b).
A post-commencement recruitment-target revision or feasibility decision without a recalculated sample-size determination or explicit revised sizing rationale; prefer item 3b.
Only states that the study was underpowered or did not reach target without reporting the original prospective calculation, planned target, or rationale for adjustment.

must_have: Explicitly report planned, performed, or absent interim analyses; an interim review of accumulating trial data; a data-based decision to continue, modify, halt, or cease the trial; or prespecified stopping, continuation, modification, or recruitment-cessation guidance. Committee involvement qualifies only when the text reports an interim data review, a resulting trial-management decision, or stated stopping guidance. Interim reassessment of a sample-size input qualifies when it is linked to a continuation, modification, or stopping decision.
not_if: Do not assign for sample-size, power, significance-level, or dropout calculations without interim reassessment linked to a trial-management decision, interim-analysis information, interim monitoring, or stopping guidance; use 7a when applicable.
Do not assign solely because the trial ended early when no interim-analysis basis, monitoring decision, or stopping guidance is reported; use 14b when applicable.

Do not assign for a committee being established, routine safety oversight, or periodic committee reports alone when there is no explicit interim data review, data-based decision, or stopping guidance.
Do not assign for a protocol or outcome change that only reports the change and does not describe interim monitoring, data-based decision criteria, or stopping guidance; use 3b or 6b when applicable.
Do not assign for final-analysis methods or results that do not describe interim analyses, interim monitoring, or stopping guidance; use 12a or results items when applicable.
7b.definition: When applicable, explanation of any interim analyses and stopping guidelines

must_have: The text states how the random allocation sequence, assignment order, or allocation-determination procedure was produced or determined.
A recognised randomisation system, allocation algorithm, adaptive probabilistic procedure, random source, randomisation list, or assignment-order procedure may satisfy the item.

A centrally operated automated response or assignment platform satisfies the item when it is reported as performing randomisation, assigning randomisation identifiers, or determining treatment allocation; it may also warrant items 8b or 10.
A contextual continuation may satisfy the item when it provides reproducibility detail for an already established sequence-generation procedure.
not_if: Do not assign when the text only says participants were randomised, with no method or contextual continuation describing sequence generation or assignment determination.
Do not assign for a deterministic non-random assignment rule, such as alternation, date-based allocation, or record-order allocation.
Do not assign when allocation ratio, blocking, stratification, or minimisation is the only information and no generation or assignment-determination approach is reported; assign 8b when applicable.

Do not assign when the text only describes concealment, packaging, distribution, release, or delivery of assignments without indicating how the sequence or assignment order was determined; assign 9 or 10 when applicable.

Do not assign when the text only identifies personnel responsible for generating, enrolling, or assigning, without a reported generation or assignment-determination approach; assign 10 when applicable.
8a.definition: Method used to generate the random allocation sequence

must_have: An explicit random-allocation detail: the randomisation type or procedure, a restriction or balancing/stratification approach, or allocation structure such as an allocation ratio, equal allocation, factorial allocation, or the number of concurrently randomised arms.
A named chance-based procedure qualifies as randomisation-type detail.
Allocation-structure or restriction detail may be established jointly by adjacent sentences when their randomisation linkage is explicit.
not_if: The text merely says participants were randomised, with no further allocation detail.
The text gives sequence-generation technology only, without describing the allocation procedure, restriction, balancing approach, or allocation structure (item 8a).
The text describes concealment mechanisms only, without randomisation-type, restriction, procedure, or allocation-structure detail (item 9).
The text identifies trial personnel only, without randomisation-type, restriction, procedure, or allocation-structure detail (item 10).
The text describes interventions or treatment groups only, without randomisation allocation detail (item 5).
Do not exclude a randomisation-linked allocation ratio solely because it may also support item 3a.
Do not assign for allocation to treatment sequences or crossover sequences alone; require an explicit randomisation type, restriction, ratio, or parallel-arm allocation structure.
Do not assign for participant-flow counts or enrolment totals, even if the number of arms is reported (item 16).
Do not assign for administrative randomisation-record fields alone unless adjacent context explicitly states a restriction, stratification, balancing method, or allocation structure.
8b.definition: Type of randomisation; details of any restriction (such as blocking and block size)

must_have: An explicit method, access restriction, controlled release, delayed disclosure, or allocation-linked pack, envelope, container, kit, label, or dispensing process that implements assignment.

The reported feature must protect, control, identify, sequence, release, or operationally handle allocation information or assigned treatment packs; a complete description of all personnel and safeguards is not required.
Numbered, serialised, or otherwise uniquely identified packs or containers qualify when they are used to select, dispense, label, or deliver assigned treatment.

A pack, container, label, or dispensing detail may qualify when immediately linked context establishes that it is part of the allocation process, even if the target sentence also supports item 10 or 11b.
An explicit statement that a central service, randomisation unit, or similar process ensures allocation concealment qualifies, even when the mechanism is briefly described.
not_if: Only random assignment is stated, with no concealment or implementation detail.
Only sequence generation is described; assign item 8a or 8b as applicable.
Only a person, unit, platform, or service administering randomisation is identified, with no stated concealment role, access-control feature, or allocation-pack process; assign item 10.
Only post-allocation blinding is described; assign item 11a.
Only appearance matching is described, without an allocation-linked numbered, controlled, or dispensing-pack process; assign item 11b.
Only generic intervention delivery is described, with no allocation-information or treatment-pack implementation feature.

An envelope, label, or assignment workflow is mentioned without a stated protective feature, controlled release procedure, serialised allocation-pack process, or explicitly linked concealment mechanism.
Concealment is mentioned only as a risk, rationale, or intended goal, without reporting how allocation access or treatment release was controlled.
Do not infer concealment merely from alternating assignment, a randomisation label, or routine opening or dispensing activity.
9.definition: Mechanism used to implement the random allocation sequence, describing any steps taken to conceal the sequence until interventions were assigned

must_have: An explicit allocation-linked operational action, control, workflow, timing/status decision, or post-randomisation implementation step.
The sentence may identify an actor, role, service, system, pharmacy, unit, or other operational entity, but naming an entity alone is insufficient.

Qualifying evidence includes enrolment-to-assignment workflow, allocation communication, allocation-code handling, allocation-linked identifier or pack handling, distribution or release of assigned materials, post-randomisation documents or arrangements, and monitoring of allocation operations.

A sentence may qualify through allocation status or timing, including eligibility-triggered randomisation, exclusion from a later randomisation, staged randomisation, or timing of assignment, when the local context clearly concerns allocation.
Indirect evidence is acceptable when an allocation artifact or downstream action clearly implements, records, controls, or follows assignment rather than merely describing treatment delivery.
A treatment reference qualifies only when it contributes to implementation of an assigned intervention or allocation-linked workflow, rather than merely describing the treatment received.
not_if: It reports only sequence-generation methodology, including a named statistician, company, software, or generator, without a separate allocation-operation or assignment-workflow role (item 8a).
It reports only randomisation design, minimisation, blocking, stratification, balancing, or allocation ratio, even if a trials unit or system is named (item 8b).

It merely states that a system was used to randomly assign participants, without describing a further allocation workflow, control action, status, or downstream implementation step (usually item 8a or 8b).
It reports concealment, storage, pack selection, or access protection solely as secrecy measures, without allocation implementation or governance information (item 9).
It gives only a treatment regimen, dose, administration procedure, prescribing decision, or treatment recipient without allocation-workflow information (item 5).
It reports only blinding or masking status; code access or code breaking qualifies only when it explicitly concerns allocation-code operation or release rather than masking alone (item 11a).
It names staff, sites, services, or committees only for recruitment, setting, measurement, outcome assessment, monitoring, or ordinary treatment delivery.
It gives eligibility checks or centre requests without an explicit randomisation, assignment, allocation-status, or allocation-workflow consequence.
It is a content-free heading or label.
10.definition: Who generated the random allocation sequence, who enrolled participants, and who assigned participants to interventions

must_have: An explicit statement that treatment identity, assignment, or other intervention-relevant information was concealed, revealed, unavailable, or known to one or more study roles after assignment.
An explicit overall or treatment-period blinding status, including absence of blinding or inability to blind, when it characterizes the trial, study phase, or treatment period.

An explicit procedure, mechanism, or event stated to maintain, implement, break, or limit blinding, including removal of identity-bearing information before outcome review when this restricts reviewer knowledge.
An explicit statement that an assessor, reviewer, or adjudicator was masked to treatment assignment or intervention-relevant information.
not_if: Do not assign for sequence generation, allocation procedures, or concealment before assignment; use 8a, 8b, 9, or 10 as relevant.
Do not assign for product appearance, taste, packaging, or matching alone; use 11b unless the text also reports knowledge restriction, trial blinding status, or a blinding-maintenance purpose.
Do not assign for outcome assessment, review, or adjudication alone without stated masking, identity restriction, or restricted treatment knowledge; use 6a when relevant.
Do not assign when masking concerns only clinical details, patient characteristics, or other non-intervention information and does not restrict treatment or assignment knowledge.
Do not assign when a blinding adjective only describes measurement conduct, a medication, regimen, or treatment option rather than trial-level status, affected knowledge, or a blinding mechanism.
Do not assign for generic use of open design terminology unless it explicitly denotes open-label or absence of blinding.

Do not assign for randomisation-code handling, allocation workflow, analyst access restrictions, or data unblinding timing unless it explicitly reports treatment blinding, a blinding code, or post-assignment knowledge restriction.
Do not assign for safety monitoring or interim review alone unless it explicitly reports masking, unmasking, restricted treatment knowledge, or preservation of a blinding code.
11a.definition: If done, who was blinded after assignment to interventions and how

must_have: Explicitly report that intervention materials, presentation, or delivery were comparable, identical, matched, or otherwise arranged to conceal treatment identity.
Comparable presentation may concern physical, sensory, formulation, packaging, container, label, or delivery characteristics.

Operational evidence may qualify when preparation, packaging, coding, testing, or distribution of treatment units explicitly supports concealment of treatment identity or comparability of intervention materials.
For administration details, report a paired or parallel delivery feature that supports masking rather than ordinary regimen information alone.

The comparator may be explicit or clearly implicit from the active/placebo or paired-intervention context, but the statement must still describe a material, presentation, or masking-related similarity.
Information may be completed across immediately contiguous sentences when the neighbouring sentence supplies the intervention or masking context.
not_if: Do not assign for statements only identifying blinded participants, staff, or assessors without intervention-material or presentation information; use item 11a when applicable.
Do not assign for dose, timing, route, ingredients, or procedures that only describe an intervention regimen; use item 5 when applicable.
Do not assign for merely naming treatment and control without comparable presentation or a substantive masking arrangement.

Do not assign when a matching placebo is merely named within a regimen or assignment description without stating what was matched or how intervention identity was concealed; use item 5 when the substantive content is regimen description.
Do not assign for treatment-pack preparation alone unless a similarity, identical-presentation, coding, packaging, testing, or masking feature is explicitly stated.
Do not assign for sequence generation, allocation concealment, or kit assignment that lacks evidence about masked intervention materials; use items 8a, 9, or 10 when applicable.
Do not assign when similarity concerns participant characteristics, baseline status, outcomes, or results rather than interventions.
Do not assign to titles, labels, or headings without substantive intervention-presentation information.
11b.definition: If relevant, description of the similarity of interventions

must_have: The sentence explicitly states a statistical test, model, estimator, analytical comparison, diagnostic procedure, curve-construction method, or statistical software-supported analysis applied to trial data or outcomes.
An explicit treatment comparison is helpful but not required when the sentence clearly describes a statistical method used for trial outcomes, covariates, or derived analytical variables.
Explicit inferential conventions governing analyses, such as test sidedness or multiplicity handling, qualify even without naming a model.
A sentence that is only a continuation may qualify when immediately local methods context explicitly identifies the statistical method that the sentence explains.

Details such as adjustment, transformations, repeated observations, clustering, interactions, or missing-data handling support assignment only when linked to an identifiable analytical procedure or model.
not_if: The text only defines, measures, classifies, adjudicates, averages, or schedules an outcome, with no statistical-analysis procedure; assign 6a when applicable.
The text only states outcome changes after trial commencement, with no statistical-analysis procedure; assign 6b when applicable.
The text only gives sample-size, power, alpha, or significance assumptions without an analysis procedure; assign 7a when applicable.
The text only describes interim monitoring or stopping rules without an outcome-analysis method; assign 7b when applicable.
The text only identifies an analysis population, protocol adherence, or assigned-group inclusion without a statistical procedure; assign 16 when applicable.

The text only defines observation eligibility, follow-up windows, censoring boundaries, event consolidation, specimen quality, measurement adjudication, or raw-value substitution, unless linked to a named statistical analysis method.
The text only lists covariates or says effects were adjusted, without identifying the model, test, or analytical operation used.
The text only reports estimates, intervals, significance values, correlations, or interaction findings as results without describing the method; assign 17a or 17b when applicable.
The text is solely an additional or subgroup-analysis report with no explicit statistical-method content; assign 12b when applicable. Do not exclude 12a merely because 12b also applies.
The text merely asserts that groups differ or were compared, with no analytical operation, metric, procedure, or statistical implementation.
12a.definition: Statistical methods used to compare groups for primary and secondary outcomes

must_have: The sentence must explicitly report a statistical procedure, analytic handling decision, model feature, adjustment, alternative analysis population, or named analysis used for an additional, ancillary, exploratory, safety, reliability, pharmacokinetic, subgroup, interaction, missing-data, multiplicity, or adjusted analysis.

The statement must provide methodological content, such as a named analysis, test, model, covariate adjustment, repeated-measures structure, imputation rule, analysis-population definition, comparison structure, or correction approach; merely naming an analysis topic or reporting results is insufficient.

For subgroup or exploratory analyses, the text must state an actual analytic action or method, not only that outcomes were presented by subgroup, that groups may be compared, or that an analysis could be performed.

Adjusted models, covariate control, confounder control, repeated-measures factors, missing-data handling, alternative estimands, and alternative analysis populations can qualify as 12b even when the same sentence also supports 12a.
A method can receive both 12a and 12b when it describes the main outcome analysis and an explicit additional-analysis component.
not_if: Do not assign if the method is clearly limited to the main primary or secondary outcome comparison and contains no explicit adjustment, alternative-analysis, handling, or ancillary component; assign 12a instead.

Do not assign a generic model, test, correlation, survival method, diagnostic-accuracy method, or regression solely because it is statistically sophisticated; it must have explicit additional-analysis scope or a qualifying adjustment or handling feature.
Do not assign if the sentence only reports subgroup or adjusted findings, effect estimates, confidence intervals, or P values without methodological content; assign 18 instead.
Do not assign if subgroup status is only used to present results or define reporting groups and no analytic procedure, comparison method, or handling decision is stated.
Do not assign if the text describes a possible, planned-in-general, or hypothetical comparison without stating that an analysis was conducted or specifying its method.
Do not assign if stratification is described only as a randomisation feature, with no analysis-stage use; assign 8b instead.
Do not assign if the text only defines outcomes or describes measurement procedures without an analysis method; assign 6a instead.
Do not assign if covariance, adjustment, or modelling is mentioned only for sample-size determination; assign 7a instead.
Do not assign if the text only refers to protocol availability or prespecification without stating an analysis or handling method; assign 24 instead.
Do not assign to titles or labels lacking substantive methodological content.
12b.definition: Methods for additional analyses, such as subgroup analyses and adjusted analyses

must_have: Explicitly report a participant count, proportion, or status that accounts for movement into, through, or out of the trial cohort or a trial group.

The accounting must concern a cohort transition such as screening or enrolment, assignment, treatment receipt or switching, completion of a protocol procedure, withdrawal, or other participant disposition.
A labelled figure or table reference qualifies when it unambiguously identifies a participant-flow or cohort-disposition display, even if the caption itself contains no numeric count.
A participant-level treatment change may qualify when it reports how many participants moved between treatment exposures or treatment states; regimen details alone do not qualify.
Group-specific counts are not required when an overall cohort count clearly represents participant progression or disposition.
not_if: Do not assign for endpoint event counts, response rates, outcome values, effect estimates, or statistical comparisons without separate cohort-transition evidence (17a, 17b, 18).
Do not assign when the only count is inclusion in an analysis set or a primary-analysis population; assign to 16 unless distinct participant-flow accounting is also reported.
Do not assign when the only information is outcome-data availability or assessment completeness; assign to 17a when it reports outcome ascertainment rather than cohort progression.
Do not assign for follow-up duration, visit timing, or observation period without participant disposition counts (14a).

Do not assign for dose level, dose escalation, adherence, allocation compliance, or intervention procedures unless the statement explicitly counts participants changing treatment exposure or cohort status (5).
Do not assign for adverse-event frequencies or safety-event counts without participant-flow or disposition content (19).
Do not assign for baseline-characteristic descriptions, disease-severity distributions, recruitment targets, or population labels without cohort-transition accounting (15).
Do not assign to a generic study-design figure or table reference unless it explicitly signals participant flow, cohort disposition, allocation, treatment receipt, or withdrawals.

Do not exclude solely because accounting is pre-randomisation or because it is co-labelled with 4a or 13b; however, losses and exclusions described only as reasons for non-participation may primarily support 13b.
13a.definition: For each group, the numbers of participants who were randomly assigned, received intended treatment, and were analysed for the primary outcome

must_have: Report participant loss, exclusion, withdrawal, noninitiation, discontinuation, death, or another event preventing continued trial participation, follow-up, or assessment after trial entry or allocation.
A reason, group-specific count, or explicit follow-up stage strengthens the label but is not required when post-entry disposition is otherwise clear.
A reported discrepancy between participants randomised or entered and participants completing study or follow-up can support item 13b when it implies post-entry non-completion.
Deaths during trial follow-up can support item 13b when they prevent further participation or assessment, including when also reported as harms.

A figure, table, caption, label, or footnote may carry item 13b when it explicitly identifies a trial profile, patient disposition display, or participant-flow artifact expected to present losses or exclusions.
not_if: The text concerns screening failure, eligibility, recruitment exclusion, non-enrolment, or prespecified exclusion before trial entry only (item 4a).
The text only reports numbers assigned, treated, completed, or analysed, with no loss, exclusion, noninitiation, discontinuation, death, or completion gap implying non-completion (item 13a).
The text only gives an analysis denominator, analysis set, specimen set, or assigned-group analysis statement without participant disposition evidence (item 16).
The text reports protocol deviations or method changes without clear exclusion from participation, follow-up, or analysis (item 3b).
The text gives a reason for ending the trial rather than reasons participants left the trial (item 14b).

The text reports adverse-event incidence, safety subgroups, or treatment discontinuation solely as a harms or outcome result, without participant-flow or cohort-disposition accounting (item 19 or item 17b).
The text only reports missing readings, missed assessments, or measurement availability without explicitly establishing withdrawal, loss to follow-up, exclusion, or non-completion.
13b.definition: For each group, losses and exclusions after randomisation, together with reasons

must_have: Explicitly report calendar date(s), a date range, or dated start/end milestone(s) that bound recruitment, participant inclusion, enrolment, randomisation, overall study conduct, or follow-up.

A calendar span qualifies when it is attached to the study or trial, recruiting or enrolling participants, randomising participants, defining the included study population, or participant completion. This remains true when the dates are embedded in a design, setting, or intervention description.
A single dated endpoint qualifies when it explicitly marks recruitment stopping, study closeout, or follow-up ending.
A duration without calendar dates qualifies only when wording explicitly presents it as realized or completed participant follow-up, not merely as a planned schedule.
not_if: Do not assign for a recruitment horizon used only for sample-size, feasibility, or operational planning; consider item 7a.
Do not exclude a calendar-bounded participant-inclusion period solely because it is prospectively framed, if it functions as the stated study recruitment window rather than a feasibility target.
Do not assign for an early-cessation rationale alone when no date or temporal endpoint defines recruitment, trial conduct, or follow-up; consider item 14b.
Do not assign for setting, site, or geography alone without a trial-period boundary; consider item 4b.
Do not assign for intervention administration timing without a recruitment, conduct, or follow-up boundary; consider item 5.
Do not assign for a scheduled outcome-assessment timepoint or monitoring window that does not define actual follow-up; consider item 6a.
Do not assign for participant counts, exclusions, or flow alone without temporal conduct bounds; consider item 13a or 13b.
Do not assign for dates unrelated to trial conduct, recruitment, inclusion, randomisation, or follow-up.
14a.definition: Dates defining the periods of recruitment and follow-up

must_have: The sentence reports an actual trial-level completion, stopping, suspension, closure, or termination and gives, or clearly links through immediate context to, the reason, trigger, or decision basis for that endpoint.

An operational action such as recruitment cessation or study-wide treatment discontinuation may qualify only when it is explicitly tied to an actual trial-level suspension, stopping, or completion decision and its rationale.
not_if: The sentence gives only recruitment or follow-up dates without a trial-level completion or stopping rationale; assign 14a when applicable.
The sentence reports recruitment stopping after target attainment but does not establish that the trial itself ended or was stopped for that reason.
The sentence describes planned completion, intended duration, or prespecified sample-size completion without reporting an actual endpoint decision.
The sentence describes prospective interim analyses, monitoring boundaries, or stopping guidance without reporting an actual stop; assign 7b when applicable.
The sentence names a committee, sponsor, or funder, or states that a sponsor ended a study, but gives neither an actual stopping reason nor a decision basis.
The sentence describes a protocol, eligibility, intervention, or outcome change without trial termination; assign 3b or 6b when applicable.
The sentence concerns individual withdrawal, treatment discontinuation, exclusion, or loss to follow-up rather than trial-level cessation; assign 13b when applicable.
The sentence gives reasons for declining participation or non-enrolment rather than why the trial ended; assign 18 when applicable.
The sentence reports target calculation or enrolment progress without an actual trial-level stopping or completion rationale.
14b.definition: Why the trial ended or was stopped

must_have: Explicitly reports descriptive characteristics of enrolled participants, randomised groups, study cohorts, or a relevant participant subgroup.

The reported characteristic may be demographic, clinical, diagnostic, symptom-related, imaging-related, biological, socioeconomic, exposure-related, disease-severity, treatment-status, or other entry-status information.

The characteristics are presented as a baseline, enrolment, entry, randomisation, pre-outcome, or cohort-profile description, either for the full cohort, treatment groups, or a clearly defined participant subset.

Narrative group comparisons and descriptive comparisons of contributors versus non-contributors, retained versus non-retained participants, or sample-providing versus non-sample-providing participants can qualify when they describe participant profiles.

An informative table title or caption that explicitly identifies demographic, clinical, baseline, patient, participant, or group characteristics qualifies even if the caption contains no numeric values.
A baseline measure may qualify alongside item 18 when the sentence both describes a participant characteristic and reports an association or other ancillary analysis.
not_if: Do not assign to eligibility requirements, licence criteria, or exclusion rules alone; use item 4a.
Do not assign to recruitment dates, retention counts, losses, or participant flow alone; use items 13a or 13b.
Do not assign to analysis counts, scan availability, denominators, sequencing availability, or analysis-set labels alone; use item 16.
Do not assign to efficacy outcomes, treatment effects, or post-treatment outcome measurements alone; use items 17a or 17b.
Do not assign to adverse-event or safety reporting alone; use item 19.

Do not assign to standalone intervention descriptions, treatment receipt, procedural delivery, or timing of treatment administration unless they are explicitly presented within a participant-characteristics profile; use item 5 when appropriate.

Do not assign to statistical associations, correlations, trends, reliability findings, or significance tests alone when they do not substantively describe baseline or cohort characteristics; use item 18 when appropriate.
Do not assign to a vague assertion that groups were balanced, similar, or comparable without actual characteristics or an informative table reference.
Do not assign to an isolated diagnosis, condition count, or participant fact unless surrounding context establishes that it is part of a baseline or cohort-characteristics presentation.
Do not assign to generic subsection titles alone; an informative characteristics-table caption may qualify.
15.definition: A table showing baseline demographic and clinical characteristics for each group

must_have: Explicitly report a participant count or proportion included in an analysis, retained for follow-up, completing the study, reaching a study stage, being evaluated, or having outcome data available
Or explicitly define the population included in an analysis, such as an intention-to-treat, per-protocol, complete-case, or original-assignment population
Original-assignment wording qualifies only when it identifies the included cohort or states that participants were included; merely stating that analyses used allocation groups is insufficient
Or identify a participant-flow, study-flow, trial-profile, or disposition display that serves as the report's participant-accounting record
Counts may be overall or group-specific; arm-specific denominators are not required
A retained, completion, stage-entry, or data-availability count may support both item 16 and participant-flow items 13a or 13b
not_if: Do not assign for statistical methods or missing-data methods alone without a stated analysis population or participant count; use item 12a or 12b
Do not assign for allocation-handling language alone when it does not identify who was included in the analysis
Do not assign for outcome results, event counts, rates, or effect estimates that do not identify the contributing, retained, or analysed population; use item 17a or 17b
Do not assign for outcome-table group sizes or captioned measurement sample sizes when they only describe compared results or laboratory measurements
Do not assign for adverse-event counts or treatment discontinuations alone when they do not account for an analysis, follow-up, or retained population; use item 19 when applicable

Do not assign for biological specimens, samples, scans, challenges, or ancillary-data subsets unless the statement explicitly defines the participant population available for the trial analysis or follow-up
Do not assign for eligibility criteria alone; use item 4a

Do not assign for isolated allocation, treatment-receipt, procedure, scan, loss, or protocol-deviation counts when they do not state a resulting retained, completed, available, or analysed population; use item 13a or 13b
Do not assign for exclusion or crossover statements used only to qualify a treatment-effect result when no resulting analysis population is stated; use item 17a
Do not use a recruitment count alone as an automatic trigger: distinguish recruitment reporting from participant accounting when the context permits
Do not treat a generic table or figure reference as evidence unless it identifies a flow, profile, or disposition display
16.definition: For each group, number of participants included in each analysis and whether the analysis was by original assigned groups

must_have: A reported finding, value, comparison, change, association, correlation, or measurement result for an analysed trial outcome or outcome-related measurement
The finding may be between groups, within a group over time, versus baseline, or an association involving an outcome-related measurement; a treatment comparison is not required
The outcome-result context may be stated in text or established by a linked results table, figure, panel, or caption
A caption or display reference qualifies when it identifies an outcome-result display and supplies analytical context, such as groups, timepoint, population, or analysis
Assign 17a in addition to 17b for binary outcome findings and in addition to 18 for subgroup, exploratory, sensitivity, adjusted, or other additional analyses that report an outcome finding
Group-specific results, a between-group estimate, statistical significance, and precision are supportive details rather than universal requirements
not_if: The text only defines, names, changes, schedules, or records outcomes without reporting findings; assign 6a or 6b when applicable
The text only describes planned or performed statistical methods without reporting results; assign 12a or 12b when applicable
The text only reports analysed population size, adherence, completion, withdrawal, or intention-to-treat status; assign 13a or 16 when applicable

The text is limited to baseline characteristics or descriptive participant information and does not report an outcome-related measurement finding, comparison, association, or correlation; assign 15 when applicable
The text reports harms or safety findings only; assign 19, while allowing 17a co-assignment when the finding is explicitly analysed and presented as a trial outcome result
The text is only a heading, caption, or display label that merely names an outcome or explains a graphic and lacks outcome-result analytical context
Do not exclude 17a solely because the finding is binary, subgroup-based, exploratory, adjusted, or otherwise additionally analysed; co-assign 17b or 18 when applicable
17a.definition: For each primary and secondary outcome, results for each group, and the estimated effect size and its precision

must_have: Explicitly reports, summarises, compares, or clearly locates a binary outcome result: an event or non-event, response status, threshold attainment, prevalence, withdrawal, recovery, death, or safety event.

The binary result may be expressed as counts, percentages, proportions, rates, risks, odds, relative effects, absolute effects, number needed to treat, or a qualitative comparison that identifies the binary outcome or its result display.
A clearly identified table, figure, caption, or referenced display qualifies when it locates binary outcome or binary safety-event results, even without a numerical result in the referring text.
Apply jointly with 17a, 19, 13b, or 18 when the same text also meets those items' criteria.
not_if: Do not assign for purely continuous outcome results, such as means, mean differences, medians, scale scores, or changes from baseline, unless a distinct binary event, responder, threshold, or occurrence result is also reported.

Do not assign for statistical significance, confidence-interval methodology, regression output, or interaction testing alone when no identifiable binary outcome result or binary-result display is provided; use 12a or 18 as appropriate.
Do not assign for a bare qualitative statement with neither an identifiable binary outcome nor a clear result-display reference; this may instead be 17a.
Do not assign for participant flow, recruitment, baseline description, or treatment-discontinuation logistics when no binary outcome or event frequency is reported; consider 13a, 14a, 15, 16, or 18.
Do not assign for a general harms mention alone. Use 19 alone when no binary safety-event frequency, comparison, or clearly identified safety-results display is conveyed.
Do not assign merely because an ancillary laboratory or immunogenicity analysis is mentioned without a reportable binary clinical or safety outcome result; consider 18.
17b.definition: For binary outcomes, presentation of both absolute and relative effect sizes is recommended

must_have: The text reports a finding from a distinct ancillary analysis rather than only an ordinary outcome comparison.

A qualifying finding may be an association, correlation, predictor or regression result, adjusted estimate, subgroup or stratum result, interaction assessment, exploratory or post-hoc result, reliability result, biomarker analysis, or separately framed descriptive/process analysis.
The content provides an observed analytic finding, estimate, distribution, classification, comparison, or analytic summary; a randomized treatment-effect estimate is not required.
For subgroup or stratified analyses, an effect-modification test is not required when a stratum-specific, subgroup-associated, or subgroup-model finding is reported.
A result-bearing table, figure, or caption can qualify when it explicitly identifies a distinct ancillary analysis or clearly labels a display of such results.
When planning status is stated, record whether the qualifying analysis was planned, post-hoc, or exploratory; planning status is not required for item 18.
not_if: The text only reports an ordinary randomized-group, nonrandomized-group, baseline, within-group, follow-up, or repeated-timepoint outcome comparison without a distinct ancillary analytic structure; assign 17a or 17b as appropriate.

The text reports a biomarker, laboratory, process, functional, or clinical outcome comparison but does not state an association, subgroup, adjusted, exploratory, or other ancillary analysis; assign 17a or 17b as appropriate.

The text only describes analysis plans, subgroup definitions, model specifications, covariate adjustment, or statistical methods without reporting findings; assign 12b when it is an additional-analysis method description.
The text defines, measures, collects, or processes an outcome without reporting an analytic finding; assign 6a when applicable.
The text reports participant flow, enrollment, allocation, follow-up status, or analysis-population counts rather than an ancillary analytic finding; assign 13a, 13b, or 16 as appropriate.
The text reports routine harms, adverse-event frequencies, or safety comparisons without an explicit ancillary analysis; assign 19.
The text merely points to a generic outcome, efficacy, or safety table or figure and does not identify an ancillary analysis or result.
The text is only a heading or label and does not identify a distinct ancillary analysis or associated result display.
18.definition: Results of any other analyses performed, including subgroup analyses and adjusted analyses, distinguishing pre-specified from exploratory

must_have: Reports an observed trial safety finding involving a concrete named clinical complication, physiologic abnormality, toxicity, or other unintended clinical manifestation.
A named harmful clinical development can qualify without formal adverse-event terminology when the trial reports it as an observed complication or abnormality.
A textual result, table, footnote, or caption can qualify when it clearly presents concrete harms findings or a harms-results display.
The finding may be individual-level, group-specific, comparative, numerical, or descriptive; group linkage and causality attribution are not required.
not_if: Only defines, prespecifies, or measures a safety outcome without reporting a finding (item 6a).
Only describes safety collection, surveillance, attribution, or review procedures without a finding (item 6a or 12a).
Only gives generic adverse-event counts, broad event summaries, or severity categories without a concrete named manifestation.
Only reports treatment cessation, withdrawal, exclusion, or loss to follow-up; use item 13b when the sentence functions as participant disposition, even if a reason is stated.
Only reports mortality, cause of death, or survival as an outcome or disposition result rather than an explicitly identified treatment-harm finding (item 18 or 13b).
Only reports efficacy or another clinical outcome without context identifying it as an unintended safety complication (item 17a or 17b).
Only states that safety was monitored or assessed without a reported finding.
Only gives general benefit-risk interpretation or future risk speculation without an observed trial safety finding (item 22).
19.definition: All important harms or unintended effects in each group

must_have: A concrete trial-specific feature that limits, qualifies, or can reasonably weaken the evidence, including design, conduct, measurement, outcome capture, sample or event information, eligibility, comparator, or analysis features.

The sentence must explicitly state, or context must clearly establish, that the feature creates bias, imprecision, inconsistency, incomplete assessment, multiplicity risk, confounding, restricted evidentiary scope, or another limitation of the reported evidence.

The limitation may be expressed indirectly through an inability to assess an important question, non-comparable measurement, recruitment or conduct difficulty, a non-prespecified analysis, or a plausible alternative explanation tied to the trial findings.
A concrete population or eligibility restriction may receive item 20 alongside item 21 when it is presented as limiting the trial evidence, not merely as an external-applicability observation.
not_if: The sentence gives only a vague limitation statement without an identifiable evidentiary constraint.
The sentence reports a routine study characteristic, procedure, assessment time, sample description, or methodological background without a stated or context-supported evidentiary consequence.
The sentence only reports allocation concealment or blinding procedures without identifying an evidentiary consequence; assign the relevant methods item instead.

The sentence only reports a non-significant finding, effect estimate, confidence interval, chance possibility, or uncertainty about benefit or harm without identifying a concrete source of inadequate information or trial constraint; assign item 17a or item 22 as appropriate.
The sentence only reports sample-size planning or a power calculation without indicating inadequate information, shortfall, or limited detection ability; assign item 7a instead.

The sentence only reports an exploratory, subgroup, adjusted, or post hoc result without identifying non-prespecification, insufficient power, multiplicity concern, or another analytic limitation; assign item 18 instead.
The sentence merely describes many tests, statistical adjustment, or analytic procedures without stating a multiplicity concern, inadequate adjustment, or resulting risk to inference.

The sentence explicitly reassures that a possible weakness was addressed, did not materially affect findings, or does not compromise validity, unless it also identifies a remaining unresolved limitation.
The sentence proposes a larger future study, further analysis, or future confirmation without identifying a limitation of the reported trial.
The sentence concerns external applicability alone, without a concrete trial restriction presented as limiting the evidence; assign item 21 instead.
The sentence interprets benefits, harms, mechanisms, prior evidence, or clinical utility without identifying a trial-specific limitation; assign item 22 instead.
The sentence describes general clinical complexity or interpretive uncertainty that is not linked to a feature of the trial evidence; assign item 22 when it is interpretation.
20.definition: Trial limitations, addressing sources of potential bias, imprecision, and multiplicity of analyses

must_have: An explicit statement that trial findings, treatment use, or study conclusions may apply, may not apply, or should be extended to a population, setting, practice context, or condition beyond the directly studied scope.

OR an explicit or clearly inferable recruitment-coverage rationale showing that eligibility breadth, low exclusion, population diversity, setting diversity, or demographic coverage supports or limits the breadth, representativeness, or real-world relevance of the findings.

OR a conclusion that expressly qualifies intended treatment use to a clinically defined target population, broader or different care context, or downstream outcome, including a stated need to confirm findings in a larger or different population.
not_if: Pure eligibility, setting, participant-description, intervention-detail, or demographic-balance reporting without a finding-level breadth, representativeness, scope, or transferability implication (items 4a, 4b, 5, or 15).
A standalone assertion that participants are representative, diverse, balanced, or similar to another group without a stated or inferable rationale about applicability of the trial findings.

An internal-validity, design, precision, bias, recruitment, exclusion, nonrepresentativeness, or untested-intervention limitation that only describes what the trial could not assess and does not connect that limitation to external use of findings (item 20).
A future-study, replication, meta-analysis, or confirmation request that does not identify a broader or different population, setting, clinical-use context, or applicability limitation.
A subgroup result, treatment-suitability statement, or effect-modification claim without an explicit intended-use or broader-scope implication (item 18 or 22).

A generic efficacy, safety, benefit, harm, policy, recommendation, or evidence-summary conclusion that merely names a population or setting but does not assert transferability, target-population applicability, or scope limitation (item 22).
Pure outcome-definition, outcome-scope, measurement, or untested-formulation reporting without an applicability implication (item 6a or item 20).

must_have: A conclusion, interpretation, implication, explanatory account, benefit-harm assessment, or contextual comparison concerning the present trial findings or a clearly locally referenced finding.

The statement may express interpretation explicitly or implicitly through a discussion-level synthesis, conclusion, explanation, clinical-use implication, safety-management implication, or comparison with relevant evidence.

The content must do more than state an isolated result: it must state or locally imply what the result means, why it occurred, how it relates to other evidence, or what it implies for treatment, safety, or practice.
A comparison with prior trials, external evidence, or mechanistic evidence qualifies when it contextualizes, confirms, contrasts with, explains, or qualifies a present-trial finding.
Benefit-harm assessment and external evidence are optional; either can support item 22 when relevant.
Consistency with reported findings is assessed against article context; the sentence need not restate the supporting result.
not_if: An isolated numerical, directional, statistical, efficacy, null-effect, correlation, or outcome result is reported without an added or locally implied interpretation; assign 17a or 17b where applicable.
Only subgroup, adjusted, exploratory, pharmacokinetic, or other additional-analysis results are reported without an explanatory or clinical implication; assign 18.
Only adverse-event counts or safety results are reported without a safety interpretation, monitoring implication, tolerability conclusion, or overall treatment implication; assign 19.
Only a study weakness, bias concern, diagnostic limitation, or imprecision concern is stated without interpreting the findings or their certainty; assign 20.
Only applicability to populations, settings, or practice is discussed without an interpretive conclusion about trial findings; assign 21.

Only background rationale, publication novelty, prior-study description, external-study result, or general mechanistic information is provided without contextualizing a present-trial finding; assign 2a when applicable.
A recommendation, standard-care assertion, treatment claim, cost statement, or mechanistic assertion has no identifiable stated or locally implied link to the present trial findings.
A mechanistic inference concerns an ancillary observation or individual case rather than interpreting a trial-level finding.
A duplicate statement is not excluded solely because of its location or repetition; assess its interpretive content independently.
22.definition: Interpretation consistent with results, balancing benefits and harms, and considering other relevant evidence

must_have: An identifiable trial-registration number or unique registry-specific identifier is explicitly reported.
A recognizable registry-specific identifier qualifies even if the registry name is not separately stated.
The identifier may appear parenthetically or within a study-description sentence.
Registration status alone is insufficient.
not_if: No identifiable trial-registration number or registry-specific identifier is reported.
Only a registry name is reported without a trial-specific identifier.
Only generic registration status is reported without an identifier.
The text only reports ethics review or committee approval; assign item 24 when protocol information is the reported content.
The text only reports protocol access or protocol availability; assign item 24.
The text only reports funding or sponsorship; assign item 25.
Do not use competing-topic content as a veto when qualifying registration information is also present.
23.definition: Registration number and name of trial registry

must_have: The sentence explicitly identifies, cites, reports publication of, or provides an access route to the full trial or study protocol. A statement that the trial or study protocol was published qualifies, even if access wording is indirect. A completeness claim is not required.
not_if: Do not assign for a procedure or intervention protocol unless it is identified as the trial or study protocol.
Do not assign for ethics, IRB, committee, or regulatory approval of a protocol unless the sentence also provides a separate protocol citation, publication statement, or access pointer.
Do not assign for amendment-only reporting without a separate protocol citation, publication statement, or access pointer; use item 3b when applicable.
Do not assign for protocol deviations; use item 13b when applicable.
Do not assign for outcome prespecification or outcome changes without trial-protocol identification; use items 6a or 6b when applicable.
Do not assign for trial registration information without trial-protocol identification; use item 23.
Do not assign for a supplement or appendix unless it is identified as containing or being the trial or study protocol.
24.definition: Where the full trial protocol can be accessed, if available

must_have: An explicit statement that the study, trial, submitted work, or a study-related activity received funding, grant support, sponsorship, financial support, material support, operational support, organisational support, or supplied study materials
OR an explicit statement identifying an organisation as the study sponsor or funder and describing its role or no-role in study design, conduct, analysis, interpretation, reporting, or publication
OR a standalone named funder or organisation list when immediately governed by a Funding, Funders, Support, Grants, or equivalent disclosure heading

Support for manuscript development, medical writing, editorial assistance, or similar study-report activity qualifies only when funding, sponsorship, or organisational support is explicitly attributed
not_if: Do not assign for affiliations, employers, employee status, addresses, or author roles alone without a funding or support attribution

Do not assign for personal conflicts, consulting, honoraria, speaking fees, travel reimbursement, stock ownership, or author payments alone unless explicitly identified as study funding or study support
Do not assign merely because a company designed the study, collected data, analysed data, interpreted results, or participated in publication decisions; require explicit sponsor or funder attribution
Do not assign for intervention delivery, dosing, storage, preparation, or administration; assign item 5 when these are intervention details
Do not assign for a product or manufacturer mention alone unless it explicitly states that the organisation supplied materials or supported the study
