Do not assign for trial registration identifiers alone; assign item 23
Do not assign for protocol-location statements alone; assign item 24
Do not assign for thanks to participants or contributors when no financial, material, organisational, or study-support attribution is made
25.definition: Sources of funding and other support, role of funders

1a__1b.rule: Use 1a for randomized-trial identification in the title and 1b for the structured abstract summary of trial methods, results, and conclusions.
1a__1b.do_not: assign any abstract content to 1a, even when it states randomization

1a__3a.rule: Title identification as randomized belongs to 1a; trial design features belong to 3a.
1a__3a.do_not: assign Methods randomization or design descriptions to 1a

examples.sentence: We performed a 90-day, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study.

This was a prospective, multicentre, double blinded, randomised trial of standard dose oseltamivir (75 mg twice a day or paediatric equivalent) versus double dose (150 mg twice a day or paediatric equivalent) for treating severe influenza.

This was an open label, parallel, one to one randomised controlled trial, conducted in four acute care hospitals (Rabin Medical Center, Petah-Tikva (192 patients); Rambam Health Care Campus (38 patients); Holy Family Hospital Nazareth (7 patients); Wolfson Medical Center (6 patients)) in Israel, between July 2007 and April 2014.

1a__8a.rule: Use 1a for a title that identifies the report as a randomised trial; use 8a for any method used to generate the allocation sequence.

examples.sentence: A statistician independent of the study team coordinated the randomisation using computer generated random numbers.

The random allocation sequence for each comparison was generated by using a specific function (-ralloc-) in Stata (StataCorp, College Station, TX) software within the clinical unit using randomly varying block sizes of two, four, and six.

To avoid predictable alternation of treatment allocation, and thus potential loss of allocation concealment, patients were allocated with a probability of 0·80 to the treatment group that would minimise the difference between the groups on the key prognostic factors.

1a__8b.rule: Use 1a only for a title that identifies the study as randomized; use 8b for Methods text describing the randomization approach or assignment restrictions, including balance procedures, strata, blocks, or chance-based allocation.

Items in the Other category, including registration, protocol, and funding, may be annotated in any section.
When relevant information appears in a table or figure, annotate its caption when available.
If no relevant caption is available, annotate the narrative sentence that refers to the relevant table or figure.
For multi-sentence captions, annotate only sentences with checklist-relevant content and not sentences that merely explain symbols or formatting.
Do not annotate summary sections unless they contain eligible information that does not appear elsewhere in the article.
Use surrounding context to resolve referents and determine eligibility, but annotate only the sentence containing the checklist-relevant statement, not context sentences alone.
For rationale, annotate at most two sentences that best explain why the study was undertaken.
For outcome-related items, distinguish prespecified primary and secondary outcomes from additional measures before assigning outcome, analysis, or result labels.
For result items, distinguish binary outcomes from non-binary outcomes before assigning the applicable result label.
Annotate limitations only when a sentence states a specific limitation, bias source, imprecision issue, or multiplicity concern, not when it makes a generic limitations claim.
Use the item list or item-status display to identify potentially missing annotations, but base each annotation on the sentence content.
If classification remains uncertain after applying the guidance, leave the sentence unannotated or seek adjudication.
Apply each item's eligibility requirements and exclusions; a topical mention alone is not sufficient evidence for annotation.
Annotate information that is explicit or unambiguously supported by the sentence and necessary context, but do not infer unstated methodological or outcome details.
For outcome results, verify the outcome type, analysis role, and reported result form before selecting a result item.
In sentences containing multiple claims, label each eligible claim but do not extend a label to adjacent clauses that lack the required evidence.
